item.title: auto progress counter shows wrong denominator when --limit is set
item.intent: When --limit N is set, the per-sprint progress line must show N as the denominator, not the total pickable item count. The denominator must reflect how many items the session will actually attempt.
item.description: In run_sprint_loop (line ~2844), the progress line is built as '$passed/${#queued_ids[@]} complete'. When 'auto done --limit 3' is run against a 20-item backlog, queued_ids has 20 entries but the session will stop after 3 successes. The user sees '1/20 complete' instead of '1/3 complete', which is misleading. The fix is to compute a display_total as min(session_limit, queued_count) when session_limit is set, and use that as the denominator.
steps: In run_sprint_loop where progress_count is built (line ~2844), compute display_total as: if [[ -n "$session_limit" && "$session_limit" -lt "${#queued_ids[@]}" ]]; then display_total=$session_limit; else display_total=${#queued_ids[@]}; fi
Replace '${#queued_ids[@]}' with '$display_total' in the progress_count assignment
Verify that without --limit, the full backlog count is still shown
Verify that with --limit 3 and 20 queued items, the denominator shows 3
Run shellcheck and confirm zero new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: Running 'auto done --limit 3' with 20 pickable items shows progress as '1/3 complete', '2/3 complete', etc.
Running 'auto done' (no limit) with 20 pickable items still shows '1/20 complete'
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings
